newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa electronic trade to woo foreigners - JSE.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa electronic trade to woo foreigners - JSE.

text.p: Plans for switching to a system of electronic share transfer would help the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) to attract more foreign investment, the head of the new project said on Tuesday.
The JSE aims to store shares in a Central Securities Depositary and record transactions and changes in share ownership electronically, replacing its current paper-based system.

Monica Singer, the project manager said in a statement that the electronic system would enhance the security and efficient settlement of the market, reducing the risk of fraud and the time delays that accompany a paper system.
"On settlement, transfer of ownership will be immediate, thereby securing all shareholder rights for investors and reduction in risks," Singer said.
The move would also give the bourse an internationally recognised clearing and settlement system, she said.
"South Africa will be in line with the leading equities markets of the world, thereby attracting foreign investment."

The system is intended to conform to a set of rules formulated by the Group of Thirty -- a committee of international financial market experts. The G30 in 1989 made nine recommendations for improving world markets' efficiency and cutting risks.
